In 1950 group leader Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples bought his first electric guitar, an amp and the tremolo effect that would help define his sound.
Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples's guitar style influenced and inspired John Fogerty, Bonnie Raitt, Ry Cooder and countless others.
Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples spent a while as a vocalist with the Trumpet Jubilees before deciding in 1948 to form a group closer to home.
At the 1972 Wattstax festival, in a jam-packed Los Angeles Coliseum, the group was still defined by Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples's cotton-field guitar sound and backwoods church singing.
